patches.title: Trade routes deliver boycotted goods to colonies (Europe stops still respect the boycott)
patches.summary: The unload loop asks skip_test (overlay 4, file 0x30B38) whether the good is boycotted for the CURRENT nation. The route code selects the ship's nation only at a Europe stop, so at a colony stop the test reads whichever nation was selected last and can refuse the delivery. This patch jumps to a 9-byte tail that keeps the skip only when the stop is Europe (999).
patches.caveat: Needs traderoute-boycott-v2-tail: alone it jumps into empty bytes. Start from the pristine EXE. The site includes 0x4121A, so an EXE with the first boycott fix (0x4121A 75DA -> 9090, withdrawn 2026-10) is refused as unexpected bytes: restore VICEROY.EXE.0f5d5b00.bak first.
patches.notes: Only the first 3 bytes change; the last 4 are checked so that the withdrawn 0x4121A fix cannot be stacked under v2. The MZ relocation word of the lcall at 0x41213 is not touched; overlay 8 has no relocation in 0x41215-0x4121B.

patches.title: Helper for traderoute-boycott-v2 (skip only at a Europe stop)
patches.asm_before: (zero padding at the end of overlay 8)
patches.asm_after: pop cx / shr ax,cl / and al,[bp-17h] / jmp 0x41218
patches.summary: ax = 1 if the good is boycotted, then AND with the high byte of the stop number (03h for Europe = 999, 00h for a colony); back to the original 'or ax,ax / jne skip' at 0x41218.
patches.caveat: Only with traderoute-boycott-v2. Uses 9 of the 11 zero bytes at the end of overlay 8 (header 0x400F0, 0x27E paragraphs, ends at 0x428D0); no relocation there.
patches.notes: Alone it is never reached and changes nothing.

patches.title: Trade routes fill part-full holds at later pick-up stops
patches.summary: The colony load loop first checks 'every hold used' and, if so, loads nothing, even when a hold is only part full. On a route with two pick-up stops, the second stop is skipped when the first one put something in every hold. This patch removes that check; the load call itself tops up a part-full hold and stops the loop when nothing more fits.
patches.verified: QEMU on one sea route and one wagon-train land route (see docs/ANALYSIS.md, 'Second bug'); many long games with trade routes in DOSBox-Daum (2026-10).
patches.notes: Not related to the boycott: the same result with the boycott bit on and off. Europe stops use a different load path (0x4124F) and are not touched.

patches.title: Stop the idle loop flattening the RNG (battle randomness)
patches.asm_before: and ah,0x7F / push ax / lcall srand / add sp,2 / retf
patches.asm_after: add [0x28EE],ax / jmp 0xC306 / (3 dead bytes) / retf / nop x3
patches.summary: The idle loop calls srand(tick) about 18 times a second, which resets the RNG state to a small, slowly rising number, so events close in time draw nearly the same value. This patch makes the idle loop ADD the tick into the state instead. srand() itself is left byte-identical, so content that seeds explicitly (colony layout, village teaching, start placement) is unchanged by construction.
patches.verified: Static checks and QEMU measurements (docs/RNG-ANALYSIS.md); many games in DOSBox-Daum (2026-10) with colony layout, village teaching and new worlds as expected.
patches.notes: MZ relocation entry 523 points at file 0xC304 (segment word of the original srand call); the DOS loader rewrites it at load time. The patch jumps from 0xC301 to 0xC306 over it.
